findings.notes: CEL policy expressions were compiled without a cost limit, so the work one expression could do was unbounded and a policy author could exhaust a shared controller. Enabling cel-go's cost limit alone does not help, because cel-go prices O(n) operations by resolved overload ID and Kyverno declares its resource variables as dyn, so every such call is billed a flat 1 unit; fixed by pricing calls by function name, refusing operations whose predicted output exceeds a size cap before they run, and metering the total cost of one request, all delivered as environment-level program options so every policy family and the legacy kyverno.io/v1 CEL path inherit them (PR #1028). That initial fix left three same-class vectors open, closed in v1.19.0-n4k.nirmata.2: lists.range allocated its whole result in one step before the post-hoc charge could bound it, now refused pre-execution by an element-count guard; a constant-pattern findAll bypassed its target-size guard because the apiserver's regex optimizer rebuilt the call node after the guard wrapped it, now shadowed so the guarded node is kept; and size() on a large string was exempt from pricing despite its O(n) scan, now charged for the scan (PR #1238).
